title: Hypatia Health - post-mortem forensics & comms draft
content:
Summary:
- Customer: Hypatia Health (HIPAA-sensitive).
- Symptom: intermittent 502s from Redwood API for text-generation route (/v1/generate) observed 2024-11-13 08:23–10:17 UTC.
- Impact: ~14 minutes of elevated error rate bucketed into 3 spikes, then degraded performance for next 90 minutes for some tenants. Hypatia saw ~3% failed requests during window; major impact to their batch-of-10 workflows.
- Current status: mitigation (fallback routing to model-variant) applied at 09:02 UTC; investigating root cause. This doc is my working scratchpad + draft customer note.

Raw timeline (notes from pager + logs):
- 2024-11-13 08:22:11 UTC — First 502 from Hypatia customer reported via SLO alert (error rate > 1.5% over 1m).
- 08:22:34 — Alert escalated to oncall (Samir).
- 08:23:02 — Samir observed increased latency + 502s in dashboard for route route-id: hypatia/tx-generate.
- 08:25:10 — Ran quick health check: curl -v to model endpoint returned 502 / upstream-read-timeout.
- 08:27:40 — Spawned additional logs from serving pod: kubectl logs -n redwood serving-pool-hypatia-0 --since=20m. See snippet below.
- 08:45:00 — Noticed a cluster-level OOM-kill on node g5-12 (kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4152 (runtime) ...). Node had transient high memory. Restarted pods rescheduled.
- 09:02:14 — Enabled policy: route hypatia -> fallback model small-quant (lower cost, compatible) for requests > 2 seconds. Error rate dropped to baseline within 3m.
- 09:30–10:17 — Continued observing occasional 502s correlated with high KV cache miss rate on warm start workloads.

Commands & snippets tried (raw):
- curl check (reproduced 502):
  curl -sv -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"hypatia-13b","input":"summarize: ..."}'
  * Received: HTTP/2 502
  * server: nginx
  * upstream-ssl: upstream-read-timeout

- kubectl probe and tail of runtime logs (serving runtime):
  kubectl -n redwood exec -it svc/debug-shell -- bash
  kubectl logs pod/serving-rt-0 -n redwood --since=60m | grep -i "kvcache" -n -C3

  ...log excerpt...
  [2024-11-13T08:24:43Z] WARN kvcache: prefix-miss count=13 seq=1432 route=hypatia/tx-generate
  [2024-11-13T08:24:43Z] ERROR runtime: exception while reading kv-cache: EOF
  [2024-11-13T08:24:44Z] WARN model-manager: backend open error: failed to mmap quantized.bin: invalid argument
  [2024-11-13T08:24:45Z] INFO fallback: queuing request for alternate-model small-quant

Hypothesis notes (ordered by likelihood):
1) KV cache corruption / partial read on startup for some serving workers. Evidence: repeated "exception while reading kv-cache: EOF" and prefix-miss spikes coincident with errors. This explains elevated latency on warm prefix-heavy workloads.
2) Model binary mismatch after a rolling deploy earlier the night before: "failed to mmap quantized.bin: invalid argument" could imply kernel flags / file backing mismatch (NFS vs local) or incompatible quantization file layout. Only some pods hit this due to staggered rollout.
3) Node-level memory pressure/OOM causing runtime to drop connections and fail to service some requests. Evidence: kernel OOM kill at 08:45 on g5-12 and GC spikes in runtime logs. Could be correlated but first errors at 08:22 precede OOM in node. So OOM may have amplified but not initiated.
4) Network flaps between control plane and worker causing KV store RPC timeouts. Less evidence but cannot be dismissed.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses (what we ran):
- Verified file checksums of quantized.bin on pods that succeeded vs failed: sha256sum quantized.bin -> mismatch on 2/8 pods. Corroborates hypothesis (2).
- Checked mount type: failing pods showed quantized.bin on a network-backed volume (nfs-provisioner) while healthy pods had local-ssd. Suggests NFS read partials under load (supports hypothesis 1+2).
- Replayed failing request against a healthy pod copy — succeeded. Replayed against mis-staged pod — reproduced 502 + kvcache EOF.
- Heap/alloc profiling of runtime process during spike: transient +30% resident memory increase leading up to OOM on node g5-12.

Temporary mitigation implemented (09:02 UTC):
- Route-level fallback to small-quant model-variant for hypatia high-latency requests.
- Marked nodes using NFS for immediate remediation candidates.
- Rolling restart and re-stage of quantized.bin from canonical artifact bucket to local-ssd for affected node pool.
- Added temporary request throttling for long-running batched jobs from Hypatia (capacity-safe throttle).

Outstanding action items (engineering):
- [Priya] Correlate deploy job that pushed quantized.bin on 2024-11-13 03:07 UTC with storage class used. (JIRA RED-8421)
- [Ethan] Add checksum validation on model-serve startup and fail fast if mismatch. (low-risk hotfix).
- [Samir] Add kvcache read-retry and stronger EOF handling + instrument counts.
- [Infra] Evaluate moving quantized artifact mounts to local-ssd for dedicated pools and add e2e test for NFS partial reads under load.
- [Product/CS] Draft customer comms and run by legal (HIPAA).

Draft customer-facing message (for Hypatia success manager/review):
Subject: Brief update — weekend forensics & next steps on 11/13 short 502 spikes

Hi Asha and Hypatia team,

Thanks again for flagging the elevated errors early this morning — we investigated and wanted to share a preliminary update and actions.

What happened (short): between 08:22–10:17 UTC on 2024-11-13, a subset of requests to your model route experienced transient 502s and elevated latency. The issue was caused by partially-staged model artifacts combined with read-path inconsistencies on network-backed filesystems in our dedicated pool. This produced KV cache read failures in a small fraction of serving workers which led to intermittent request failures.

What we did:
- Immediately routed high-latency requests to a compatible fallback model to restore traffic and reduce errors (09:02 UTC).
- Re-staged model artifacts to local storage and restarted affected workers.
- Implemented additional throttle protection for long batch jobs during remediation.

Next steps (engineering):
- We will add startup checksum validation to prevent partially-staged artifacts from entering the fleet.
- We will harden kvcache read error handling and add retries/instrumentation.
- We'll evaluate storage-class changes for dedicated pools to avoid network-backed partial reads.

Impact to you: During the incident you saw ~3% failed requests across the 1.5-hour window; after we applied the fallback at 09:02, error rates returned to baseline within ~3 minutes. We will follow up with a full post-mortem and any SLO credit calculations after completing the forensics.

If you'd like, we can arrange a short call to walk through specifics and timelines.

Thanks,
Priya (oncall, eng-serving-runtime)

Notes / questions for internal review meeting:
- Does release pipeline guarantee atomic publish of quantized artifacts? If not, add publisher locks.
- Should we require local-ssd for quantized models above X params? (cost vs reliability).
- Can CS/legal prepare a HIPAA-safe summary and approve the draft above?

Personal scratch TODO (low-priority):
- Run a targeted e2e test to simulate partial-read on nfs (use fio + small-block random reads) against serving binary.
- Add duration histogram for kvcache-read latency to Grafana.
- Follow up with infra on node g5-12 memory pressure root cause (gpu driver vs model memory leak).

End of notes.

-- Priya Nair (working draft)
